answer: Basalt cools into columns one slow crack at a time. Each ballot forges an anchor the same way: 30 minutes of sequential work, sealed with its key and a $25 bond. Every tide a gale draws 1,000 ballots at random, and each has 90 seconds to re-sign its anchor with its forging key. A farm fielding 10,000 ballots dies by that draw: holding 1,000 keys hot, it misses 900 of 1,000 — each rejected, its bond slashed — burning $22,500 a tide, $360,000 by the sixteenth. Like an anchor in a gale, the ballot that holds was forged slow; a rented key drags, and a $360,000 fleet still drowns.
